propositions: Two reliability tests consume multi-second wall time (15s and 9s respectively) due to production-scale real-time values (10s low-speed window, 1s per-attempt deadline, real retry sleeps) despite contracts about throughput, retry schedule, and process cleanup rather than elapsed time.
The snapshot-fetch test must inject a 1s low-speed window while keeping the real loopback socket and above-floor byte pacing for more than one complete window, asserting non-stall semantics.

The ACLI subprocess test must inject sub-second call/grace/drain values through existing seams, record the exact logical retry schedule [2, 4] without sleeping, launch exactly _MAX_ATTEMPTS real child sessions, record each parent-side PID, and poll until all PIDs are absent.
Production timeout, stall, grace, drain, attempt, and backoff defaults must remain byte-unchanged with no wall-clock pass thresholds, skips, xfails, or runner changes.
